title: Schedule of Optional Extras Sold on a Given-Up Booking — Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
**Air Ticket Fare Brands — optional extras sold on a booking the traveller has given up.**

What comes back of the optional extras sold on the booking follows what the airline did to the itinerary.

- Where a notice standing on the booking records that the airline cancelled a segment and an optional extra has been sold on the booking, the optional extras are added to the amount returned at what they were charged.
- Where no notice standing on the booking records that the airline cancelled a segment and an optional extra has been sold on the booking, the optional extras are added to the amount returned at the first checked bag rate of the fare brand held, counted once for each optional extra sold.
- Otherwise nothing of the optional extras is added to the amount returned.

**First checked bag rate by fare brand**, in US dollars:

| Fare brand | First checked bag rate |
| --- | --- |
| Basic Economy Lite | 40.00 |
| Economy Saver | 35.00 |
| Economy Classic | 35.00 |
| Economy Flex | 30.00 |
| Premium Economy Select | 30.00 |
| Business Saver | 30.00 |
| Business Flex | 30.00 |

**Annotations to the lines above.** Take, on hypothetical figures, a booking held on Basic Economy Lite carrying two optional extras sold, charged at 55.00 and 45.00 US dollars, with no notice standing on it recording an airline cancellation of a segment: the first checked bag rate of Basic Economy Lite is 40.00, counted once for each of the two extras, so 80.00 is added to the amount returned, whatever the extras were charged. Had a notice recording that the airline cancelled a segment stood on that booking, the two extras would instead be added to the amount returned at what they were charged, 100.00 in all.

Where no optional extra has been sold on the booking, nothing of the optional extras is added to the amount returned, whether or not a notice recording an airline cancellation of a segment stands on it.
